prologue.title: Halloween in the village
prologue.narrator: Some stories begin with a whisper, not a scream.
prologue.text:
Tonight is Halloween.

You're in costume, Aikito wears a tiny witch hat slightly crooked, and the candy bucket is already heavy.

Windows glow with carved pumpkins.

But at the end of the street, the grey house stays dark.

The grown-ups say a ghost lives there.

A kid from the neighborhood whispers:

*« Yesterday I heard a « Boo »… but it sounded like crying. »*

Aikito sniffs the air.

*« Real villains smell like thunder. That smells like library dust. »*

quartier.title: Candy and rumors
quartier.narrator: You can celebrate and still keep one ear open.
quartier.text:
You knock on three doors.

Candy drops into your bucket.

Laughter rises in the street.

Then, between two houses, a soft sound arrives:

*« Boo… »*

It's not a shout.

It's smaller than a cat.

Shyer than thunder.

Aikito pricks up his ears.

*« Did you hear that? It wasn't to scare people. It was to call for someone. »*

choices.text: Follow the sound to the grey house

maison_grise.title: In front of the grey house
maison_grise.narrator: A house without light isn't always a house without someone inside.
maison_grise.text:
The grey house stands before you.

The shutters are closed.

A thin orange glow slips through a gap in the curtain.

*« Boo… ? »* the voice repeats, very low.

Aikito sits calmly on the first step.

*« If you want, we can just knock. Ghosts don't always want to scare people. Sometimes they just want to be heard. »*

choices.text: Knock gently with a candy in your hand

peur_passage.title: One step back
peur_passage.narrator: Stepping back isn't mean. Sometimes it's how your body says « not yet ».
peur_passage.text:
Your heart beats fast.

The door creaks just a little.

Behind it, something white and round hides right away.

*« S-s-sorry! »* says the voice. *« I didn't mean to… I just wanted to… »*

It fades, like a candle blown out.

Aikito looks at you without judging.

*« Know what I heard? Not « go away ». More like « please stay ». »*

choices.text: Go back and hold out a candy toward the door

rencontre_boo.title: Boo
rencontre_boo.narrator: A ghost isn't always a shadow. Sometimes it's just someone you can't see clearly yet.
rencontre_boo.text:
The door opens a crack.

A small round ghost floats at knee height.

He's white like a clean sheet, with two big dark eyes a little wet.

*« My name is Boo, »* he says. *« Nobody walks by on Halloween night. So I learned to say « Boo » because… that's what ghosts do, right? »*

He lowers his head.

*« Except everyone runs. Nobody stays. »*

Aikito wags his tail.

*« Ghosts are allowed to be scared too. »*

choices.text: Offer him a candy and stay a while
Teach him to say hello instead of « Boo »

partager_bonbons.title: One candy for two
partager_bonbons.narrator: Sharing is sometimes the simplest kind of magic.
partager_bonbons.text:
You hold out a pumpkin-shaped candy.

Boo hesitates, then takes it with two transparent hands.

*« Nobody ever gave me one, »* he whispers. *« Because ghosts can't knock on doors… »*

You offer your bucket.

*« We could go together. You hide behind me. And if someone gets scared, we explain. »*

Boo glows — not bright, just a little, like a night-light.

*« Really? »*

apprendre_bonjour.title: Something other than « Boo »
apprendre_bonjour.narrator: Learning a new way to say hello is giving fear a second chance.
apprendre_bonjour.text:
You step inside with Aikito.

The living room smells a bit of wax and old books.

Boo floats in the middle of the room, embarrassed.

*« Hello, my name is Boo, »* you say slowly.

Boo repeats:

*« Boo… my name is Boo… uh… Hello, my name is Boo! »*

He hides behind a cushion.

*« That's weird. You can hear my voice. But nobody screams. »*

Aikito claps with his paws.

*« Weird is the start of « different ». Not « dangerous ». »*

choices.text: Encourage him to try again at the window

halloween_ensemble.title: Three in the street
halloween_ensemble.narrator: A party grows brighter when no one is left outside.
halloween_ensemble.text:
Boo hides behind your coat.

At the first door, a lady jumps… then laughs.

*« Oh! A shy ghost! Here are two candies — one for you, one for your invisible friend. »*

Boo's eyes go wide.

*« She talked to me. »*

Farther on, kids from the neighborhood come closer.

Nobody runs.

They hold out their buckets.

Boo murmurs:

*« I thought Halloween was for scaring people. »*

choices.text: « No. It's for daring to meet each other. »

lecon_douce.title: Hello, village
lecon_douce.narrator: A little courage repeated becomes, over time, a bright light.
lecon_douce.text:
Boo moves to the window.

Outside, children pass with their lanterns.

He breathes — or tries to.

*« Hello! My name is Boo! »*

His voice trembles, but it holds.

A little boy raises his hand.

*« Hello Boo! Want to see my pumpkin? »*

Boo looks at you, amazed.

*« They didn't leave. »*

Aikito rests his head against your leg.

*« No. Because you stayed. Sometimes that's the real magic of Halloween. »*

choices.text: Open the door and greet with him

fin_partage.title: The house that glows
fin_partage.narrator: What seemed scary was mostly lonely.
fin_partage.text:
Boo's bucket is full — of candy, of names, of smiles.

When you walk him home, the grey house no longer looks abandoned.

A pumpkin glows in the window.

Boo waves at you.

*« Thank you, {{player}}. I used to think you had to shout to exist. Now I know that sometimes sharing is enough. »*

Aikito yawns.

*« Official dog philosopher moral: one shared candy beats ten « Boos » that make people run. »*

You head home smiling.

Halloween goes on — but the grey house isn't afraid of the dark anymore.

fin_bonjour.title: A ghost with friends
fin_bonjour.narrator: Kindness opens doors that fear kept shut.
fin_bonjour.text:
Children sit on the grey house steps.

Boo shows them how to float without tipping the juice glasses (almost).

He still says *« Boo »* once, out of habit — everyone laughs, him included.

*« It's okay to have been scared, »* Boo says at the end. *« What matters is trying something else afterward. »*

You put away your bucket.

The moon draws a soft halo above the roof.

Aikito concludes:

*« Ghosts, children, dogs in witch hats: we all need someone to dare knock on our door — gently. »*
